observations.behavior: Documentation update: The hunk P1.F1.H1 changes the instruction for the AI agent regarding how to use the `get_events_around` tool. It replaces the instruction 'call it up to {{ tool_budget }} times' with 'You get up to {{ tool_budget }} rounds of lookups... A round costs the same whether you ask for one moment or several, so ask about every moment you are unsure of at once rather,
observations.code_quote: You get up to {{ tool_budget }} rounds of lookups per task. A round costs the same whether you ask for one moment or several, so ask about every moment you are unsure of at once rather than spending a round on each. {% if tool_budget < default_tool_budget %}Rounds are scarce here, so spend them on the moments that decide your answer: always look up the moment where you judge whether the user succeeded, failed, or hit friction, which are easy to misread from the video alone, and skip moments that would not change your verdict.{% else %}Use the rounds liberally — cover any moment that looks interesting, and always the one where you judge whether the user succeeded, failed, or hit friction, which are easy to misread from the video alone.{% endif %} `$rageclick` (the same element clicked again and again) and `$dead_click` (a click that changed nothing) are the highest-signal friction events: treat them as ground truth, concluding one only when `get_events_around` confirms it at that video time, not from interaction bursts on tabs, dropdowns, or other re-clickable controls.
